newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds mostly flat, light selling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds mostly flat, light selling.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were broadly unchanged as market participants were somewhat defensive on Wednesday, mortgage experts said.
One Ginnie trader in New York said there was light selling of Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent coupons earlier in the session.
"We actually had a small seller of some 8.0s...but not too many bonds," he said. Market players had bid for them "quite aggressively" yesterday, he said.
By 1400 EST/1900 GMT, overall prices of mortgage-backeds were flat to 1/32 higher.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent paper was up 1/32 at 100-20/32 bid, yielding 121 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.

Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper were 1/32 higher as well, at 100-19/32 bid and 100-26/32 bid, respectively. The five-year Treasury note was unchanged at 99-19/32 bid to yield 6.72 percent and the 10-year Treasury note was up 1/32 to yield 6.87 percent.
Traders said many market players were quiet ahead of Friday's March employment report, which generally influences monetary policy expectations.

Looking ahead, many Wall Street economists expect more Fed tightening in the near term, which would flatten the Treasury yield curve. And a flatter yield curve would mean wider mortgage spreads, said BZW Securities Inc mortgage analyst Cynthia Rivera.

"That would hurt mortgages," Rivera said. As the belly of the yield curve flattens, such as in three-year and five-year Treasuries, mortgages that price off those securities would underperform as well, she said.
